radio_broadcasts.message: Civil Register, 88.5. Good morning. Dust advisory in effect through midday — close your intake valves before you boil water. Sector nine water station opens at the sixth hour. Bring your card. The queue will close at capacity. That is all.

Civil Register, 88.5. A reminder from the Bureau of Dose Records: quarterly thyroid readings are mandatory for all registered adults. Unrecorded persons cannot claim medical priority. The clinic in the east annex opens tomorrow at dawn. Bring your dose card.

Civil Register, 88.5. Community notice. The eastern purification cistern is under maintenance through the third day. Draw your water from the district canteens only. Boiling does not neutralize chemical runoff. Use the tablets. We have enough tablets.

Civil Register, 88.5. The Registry of Persons is accepting updated residence cards at window four. If you have moved or taken in unregistered members, the window is open until the afternoon bell. Unregistered occupants are not covered under the grain allocation. This is a courtesy notice.

Civil Register, 88.5. A cold front is moving in from the north ridge. Temperature is expected to drop eight degrees by nightfall. All outer shelters should verify heating fuel and seal their exhaust dampers before dark. We do not expect this to be a long cold. We have been wrong before.

Civil Register, 88.5. Notice from the district authority: movement through the eastern checkpoint is suspended pending clearance of a road obstruction. Travelers with Garrison transit papers should report to the south gate. All others wait. We will announce when the road is clear.

Civil Register, 88.5. Fuel convoy to the outer ring departs at first light. If you have a depot requisition stamped in the last ten days, report to the motor yard before the sixth hour. Unsigned manifests will not be loaded. The convoy does not make return trips.

Civil Register, 88.5. The census carriers report movement on the outer road that does not match registered caravan schedules. The district authority has been notified. Until clearance is issued, all private travel east of the viaduct is suspended. This is a safety measure.

Civil Register, 88.5. Radiation ward at the district infirmary is at capacity. Persons presenting with nausea, hair loss, and skin blistering are asked to report to the overflow tent at the outer yard rather than the main entrance. Triage will see you there. Please do not crowd the corridor.

Civil Register, 88.5. All unregistered persons residing in zones four through nine are asked to present themselves at the Bureau of Persons by the end of the seventh day. The Bureau does not arrest. It counts. But what it does not count, it cannot protect. Consider this carefully.

Garrison Forward Command, 102.1. EMERGENCY. Fallout plume detected over the industrial quarter. All persons in sectors three and five are ordered to shelter in place immediately. Seal your doors. Close your vents. Do not go to the water point. A Garrison unit is en route with clean water. Stay inside.

Garrison Forward Command, 102.1. This is not a drill. Multiple detonations have been confirmed in the outer sectors. All non-essential personnel proceed to designated hardened shelter. Your shelter assignment is on your registry card. If you do not have a card, go to the gymnasium on the main road. Move now.

Garrison Forward Command, 102.1. Radiation readings above threshold in the lower residential districts. Evacuation corridors are marked in yellow. Do not use the main boulevard — vehicles are blocking it. Use the canal path. If you have someone who cannot walk, mark your door with a red strip and a Garrison runner will come for them.

Garrison Forward Command, 102.1. Reservoir four is confirmed compromised. Do not drink the tap. Boiling is not sufficient for chemical contamination. Garrison distribution trucks are staging at the old market square with purification tablets. One pack per adult, half pack per child. Bring your card.

Garrison Forward Command, 102.1. Attention to all sheltering in the outer ring: Garrison reclamation units are moving toward your position. They are on foot. ETA unknown. Stay in your shelter. Light a signal fire on your roof if you have medical emergencies. Do not come out to meet them — the route is not yet clear.

Garrison Forward Command, 102.1. Ration authority notice. Standard protocol is in effect. Report to your district center at first light with your identification card. The Garrison allocates one hot meal per adult per day and a dried supplement for children. Medical cases take priority at the dispensary window. No exceptions to card requirement.

Garrison Forward Command, 102.1. Health notice. Radiation sickness presents as nausea, fatigue, bleeding gums, and hair loss within days of high exposure. If you have these symptoms, go to the medical station on the north concourse. Do not wait. Early intervention is the difference. Take your iodine tablets if you have them.

Garrison Forward Command, 102.1. Security notice. Unauthorized looting in the southern district has resulted in two civilian deaths. Garrison patrols are active after dark. Curfew is in effect from eight in the evening until six in the morning. The Garrison does not enjoy enforcing this. Comply and we will not need to.

Garrison Forward Command, 102.1. Weather warning. A fallout storm front is tracking from the industrial corridor. Arrival estimated in five to seven hours. The Garrison requests all persons seal their shelters immediately. Turn off forced-air ventilation. Fill your water stores now, before the storm. This is not a drill.

Garrison Forward Command, 102.1. Relay disruption in the eastern sectors has interrupted civil communications. If you are in zones six, seven, or nine and cannot reach the main frequency, the Garrison is monitoring 91.3 and 95.7 as auxiliary channels. Your district officer knows the alternate procedures. Trust your local chain.

Field intercept, 95.4. Artillery impact zone: industrial quarter, grid reference quadrant forty-seven by eighty-two. All persons in that grid take cover and remain below ground. Garrison battery is returning fire. The exchange is expected to last twenty minutes. Do not leave shelter during the exchange.

Field intercept, 95.4. Vehicle column bearing north on the old highway. Identity unclear — no transponder codes detected. Speed suggests loaded trucks. Garrison checkpoint alpha has been notified. If you are traveling that road, stop and wait. Do not be the reason an ambush starts.

Field intercept, 95.4. Unidentified aircraft sighted tracking west to east at low altitude. No identification markings visible from the ground. Garrison has logged the sighting. If you hear engine noise, stay indoors and away from windows. This is precautionary. We do not know whose it is.

Field intercept, 95.4. Reconnaissance indicates a fortified camp being established in sector nine near the old water treatment facility. Estimated numbers: thirty or more. The Garrison is classifying this as a contested zone pending identification. Scavenger and civilian transit through that area is advised against.

Field intercept, 95.4. Medical evacuation request transmitted from field station gamma. Multiple high-dose exposure casualties. Requesting clean transport with sealed cabin. If any caravan operator has a sealed vehicle and is within range of sector six, please respond on this frequency. Standard compensation applies.

Field intercept, 95.4. Supply convoy ambushed on route delta between the viaduct and the eastern relay station. Three vehicles stopped, two incapacitated. The goods — medical, not food — are at risk. Garrison element responding. Civilians in the area are advised to leave the route until the situation resolves.

Field intercept, 95.4. Chemical residue detected near the old processing plant in sector three. Origin unknown — could be industrial runoff, could be deliberate release. Readings are elevated but not immediately lethal. Persons in that area: cover your airways, move upwind, report your location. Garrison is dispatching a hazmat pair.

Field intercept, 95.4. Night patrol reported contact with an armed group at the east trench line at approximately two in the morning. Exchange of fire lasted several minutes. One friendly casualty, condition unknown. The group withdrew east. Garrison is not pursuing in the dark. Light-discipline rules apply until morning.

Field intercept, 95.4. Fire mission in progress. Artillery battery seven adjusting coordinates. Danger close to the outer perimeter. All Garrison forward elements acknowledge and clear the target corridor. Civilian shelters near the east ridge wall — move to your secondary interior positions now.

Field intercept, 95.4. Strategic situation in the outer sectors has deteriorated faster than anticipated. All forward outposts are ordered to hold position and conserve ammunition. Do not initiate engagements. The chain of command is intact. Orders will come. Hold.

This is an automated station. Radiation monitoring post Kestrel-7. Current readings: 1.4 roentgens per hour at the probe. 1.4. This station transmits every six hours without human oversight. If readings are consistent, no personnel are en route. End.

This is an automated station. Emergency water protocol, broadcast seven. Boil all surface water for ten minutes minimum. Add purification compound at three drops per liter. Rest thirty minutes before consumption. Chemical contamination requires a second treatment cycle. This message repeats every four hours.

This is an automated station. Shelter locator signal, type seven. If you can hear this frequency, you are within three kilometers of a designated hardened shelter. Refer to your civil registration card, reverse side, for the sector map. The shelter is marked with a diagonal orange stripe. End of message.

Automated medical advisory, loop four. Iodine tablets protect the thyroid only when taken before or immediately after exposure. They do not reverse damage. They do not treat sickness. If you are already symptomatic, iodine will not help you. Go to a medical station. Do not waste tablets on the already-ill when the unexposed still need them.

Automated food safety advisory. Sealed cans with intact seams remain safe indefinitely. Discard cans that are swollen, weeping, or have opened seams. Do not taste to test. Do not smell to test. Botulism has no odor. The rule is simple: if the seal is broken, it is garbage. No exceptions.

This is automated radiation monitoring post Kestrel-7. Sensor log — [DATA CORRUPTED BEYOND RECOVERY]. Sensor array is presumed intact. Next scheduled transmission in six hours. If this message has been received three times without a human response, the area is likely uninhabited. This station will continue to broadcast.

Automated shelter maintenance reminder, cycle forty-three. Air filtration indicators must be checked weekly. Indicator red means replace. Indicator orange means within two weeks. Do not run a shelter on a failed filter in fallout conditions. The carbon element goes before the HEPA mesh. Log your replacement date.

Automated weather station, loop twelve. Nuclear winter conditions persist. Average surface temperature this cycle: minus eleven degrees. Expect extended ice coverage through the northern approach roads. Minimum heating fuel per person per day: two point four kilograms of coal equivalent. Conserve. The cold does not have a schedule.

This is an automated survivor locator signal. If you are hearing this broadcast, transmit your location on 99.0. This station logs transmissions automatically. Rescue teams are dispatched when resources and security allow. Transmission does not guarantee rescue. But silence guarantees nothing. Transmit.

Automated medical protocol, loop eight. Radiation sickness management without clinical support: rest, oral hydration, and isolation of vomiting persons from food preparation areas. Potassium iodide if pre-exposure. Prussian blue if ingested contamination is suspected and the compound is available. This station does not have medical supplies to distribute.

Seven. Three. Nine. One. Five. Eight. Two. Four. Six. Zero. Seven. Three. Nine. One. Five. Eight. Two. Four. Six. Zero. [The sequence repeats without deviation for approximately eleven minutes. No voice identifies the source. The rhythm is precise enough to be mechanical, but the breath between groups is unmistakably human.]

Alpha. Nine. Nine. Bravo. Seven. Three. Charlie. One. Five. Delta. Eight. Two. Echo. Four. Six. Foxtrot. Zero. Seven. Golf. Three. Hotel. Nine. [Encoded phonetic transmission. No preamble. No callsign. The voice is calm and unhurried, as if reading a familiar text. It begins again at the end without pause.]

Niner. Niner. Niner. Break. Break. Break. Station Echo to whoever is copying. Cache confirmed at grid forty-seven by eighty-two. It is dry, it is sealed, and it is inside the derelict grain elevator. The padlock is the old kind. Bring a number four pick or a pry bar. Good luck out there.

One. One. Two. Three. Five. Eight. Thirteen. Twenty-one. Thirty-four. Fifty-five. Eighty-nine. One-forty-four. [The Fibonacci sequence, broadcast without commentary. After the last number, a long pause. Then, quietly, the same voice: 'Still here.' And the sequence begins again.]

Mike. Romeo. Kilo. Seven. Seven. Three. Lima. November. Papa. Two. Two. Nine. Oscar. Quebec. Romeo. Five. Five. One. [Military phonetic sequence. The voice is young — possibly a teenager who learned procedure from an older adult. It skips a syllable on 'Quebec' and corrects itself without acknowledgment. The sequence continues regardless.]

Is anyone out there? This is — my name is Sela. I'm in the old water board offices on the south road. I have two other people with me. One of them is sick — the throwing-up kind, not the radiation kind, I think. We have water, we have a little food. What we don't have is medicine. If you can hear this, please — we're in the building with the blue tiles. The ones that aren't broken.

Warning. This is a personal warning from someone who went north and came back, which not everyone did. The road past the cooling towers is gone. There is no road. There is rubble and hot ash and the dosimeter pegs in thirty seconds flat. We lost Dani there. I am telling you so you do not lose yours. Do not go north. Find another way or do not go at all.

This is the Westside Collective on 101.3. We have established a working community in the old library building at the edge of the residential quarter. We have food, water through a slow filter, and a doctor — a real one, the bone kind, not the feeling-better kind. All survivors are welcome. We have space. We are trying to be the thing that holds. Find us.

Day forty-seven. Still transmitting. Found an unlooted pharmacy in sector six — the whole back stockroom was sealed behind a collapsed shelf. Antibiotic packs, burn dressings, two working blood pressure cuffs. I took what I could carry and marked the door with a red X so others can find the rest. The dosimeter is clicking more than it should. I am not thinking about that right now.

To whoever is running 102.1 — we hear you. Every morning we hear you, clear as anything. We do not know if you are Garrison or something else. We are not asking you to identify yourself. We are asking you to hear us back. We have forty-three people in a converted freight depot and no way to reach the city. If you can, please respond on this frequency. We will be listening all day.

Eight-two-six. Nine-zero-one. Delta-seven. Sequence: four, four, one, nine, two. Standby for encrypted coordinate handshake. [A secondary tone pulse follows — three long, two short, three long. The tone sequence holds for forty seconds, then cuts to static without announcement.]

Sub-tier reserve manifest check, sector nine, ledger volume four. Rations logged at four hundred units. Filter stock: eighty cartridges. Medical consignments: sealed and locked under the quartermaster's witness signature. Awaiting authorized key from the district office. This channel is encrypted. If you are not the quartermaster and you are hearing this clearly, report the breach.

Command cadre rotation. Terminal alert. All outposts acknowledge. Dead-drop shelter protocol is active at waypoint November. The microfilm index is the third drawer from the bottom. This message has been transmitting for — [corrupted timestamp]. If the command cadre is alive, they should have already authenticated. If they have not authenticated, proceed under Standing Continuity Order Seven.

Wildlife net, 88.5. Thaw run underway — grazers coming down off the high ground in strings of six and more. If you're running snares, run them now; the window closes when the bloom starts. Water crossings at dusk, mind your footing.

River net, 96.1. The water's awake — mirror carp moving down the estuary in numbers nobody has logged since before. Wet ground only, and the gulls will show you where. Salt what you can't eat. The ice takes it all back soon enough.

Station notice for the lowlands. Insect front moving in from the floodplain — cutworm and moth brood riding the damp air. Screen your trays, seal your grain, pick your rows by lamplight. This one eats before it flies on.
Advisory, 88.5. Game counts are down across the winter range and the predators know it. Wolves working the fence lines after dark. Keep the kill meat off the perimeter and your stocks latched.
Distress signal detected on 88.3 MHz. Fragmentary voice transmission. Female voice, signs of distress. References rail depot and trapped position. Signal strength increasing over three-day window.
Distress signal detected on 156.8 MHz. Male voice, signs of injury. References route 6 and burned gas station. Mentions trade goods. Two-day clarity window.
Automated signal detected on 129.6 MHz. Mechanical tone repeating every thirty seconds. No voice. Five-day clarity window. Source unknown.
Signal detected on 192.4 MHz. Mentions fuel cache and unguarded supplies. Two-day clarity window. Signal pattern suspicious — no variation in transmission.
Distress signal detected on 333.6 MHz. Claims to be from Grange Hall settlement. Three-day clarity window. Voice pattern inconsistent with known settlement members.
Encrypted burst detected on 701.3 MHz. Military encryption pattern. Five-day clarity window. Contains coded coordinates and authentication sequence.
Distress signal detected on 812.5 MHz. Child's voice. References school and collapsed ceiling. Two-day clarity window. High urgency.
Military distress signal detected on 901.2 MHz. Sergeant identification, references patrol six and ambush. Three-day clarity window. Mentions wounded and low ammunition.

Voice of the Vitrified Crater, 104.2. [A deep chamber; words slower than speech.] The heat went through the valley in one second and left the floor of it as glass. Consider that. A mirror the size of a district. Everything at the rim can see itself in the place where the town was. We do not say the glass is holy. We say it is honest, and that it took a fire to make a surface that would hold this valley's face.

The liturgy of counts, 104.2. [Voices in unison, uneven.] We read the numbers at the sixth hour. Four point one at the north rim. Six point eight in the culvert. Two point two where the children may walk. A number spoken in a room is a number somebody heard; a number nobody heard is only weather. Read your own counts tonight, whoever you are. Say the number, then say the day. That is the whole prayer.

From the sealed chamber beneath the rim, 104.2. [The recording is older than the voice introducing it.] This was cut eleven winters ago in a room nobody has opened since. Twenty-six names, sung in the manner of the lower hall. If your name is among them, the chamber is wrong and you are welcome at the rim. If it is not, you are the reason we still transmit this. We will not edit the tape. The tape is the record.

Sermon of the second sun, 104.2. [One voice, close, patient.] Nine of us saw it. It was not beautiful and we will not tell you it was. It was a light that made shadows out of things that never had them — the fence, the wheel, the hand. We have preached it eleven years and the newest among us still ask what we worship. Answer: nothing. We are keeping the hour. The ones who kept it before us are the shadows on the fence.

Notice from the rim, 104.2. [Wind; a bell struck twice.] Walk to the crater and bring a name. Leave it at the marker stones. Do not bring food; we have food. Do not bring fuel; we will refuse it. We will not ask what you believe, and we will not ask again on the way out. The stones are north, below the wire, where the count is lowest. Come in daylight. We are not what the roads say.

Roll call, 104.2, read by the keeper of the stair. [Each name is followed by a pause for one breath. The pauses are the point.] Alderman. Present in the glass. Brigg. Present. Corra, who sang the lower hall. Present. Esme, aged nine. Present in the glass. [Thirty-two more follow.] That is the hall as it stood. If you hear a name you carried, you are not the only one carrying it, and the rim has a stone with room on it.

The Open Airwaves, 91.3. Morning lesson. [Chalk taps a slate twice.] If a child is near this speaker, sit beside them; they will ask you the sounds and you should know them too. Today: the letter that opens the mouth wide, and the letter that closes it. Say them with me. [A pause; a room of perhaps four people, wind in the mast.] Good. That is reading. Reading is not the paper. Reading is the sound somebody agreed to.

Arithmetic for shelters, 91.3. [Pencil on paper.] Division, and it is not an abstraction. Eleven people, forty tins, six days. How much does each eat daily, and what is left over? Do it before I say it — whoever cannot do this sum will be told what the sum decided. [A pause; somebody errs and is corrected kindly, on air.] Now use your real numbers, and write the remainder down. The remainder is where the arguments live.

Lineman's hour, 91.3. [Wind; tools on a metal tray.] You are listening to a mast in weather; this is the sound of the job. Today: the splice that survives winter. Strip back two fingers, not more. Twist with the grain, never against — against it the wire work-hardens and fails in the cold. Bind, seal, pull hard once. If it holds the pull it holds the season. If you hear this on a repaired set, somebody did that for you.

Well-tenders' lesson, 91.3. [Chalk.] If your water comes green, do not fear it and do not drink it. Green at the well mouth after storms is usually mineral, often harmless. Green with a film that breaks when you stir is different. Boiling kills what lives; the mineral stays. Stir it, watch the film, smell the cup, note the day. Three days of notes is a diagnosis. One frightened evening is only a rumor.

Geography of home, 91.3. [A stiff map unfolded.] You cannot navigate the valley as it is without the valley as it was. The rail cut ran north from the siding. The water tower stood where the count is highest now — weather and low ground. The quarry turn is where the road crust fails when wet. Name three features you can see from your own door, to whoever shares it. A named place is a place you can give directions in.

End of the morning block, 91.3. [The chalk is put down.] Before I close, the register — the part that outlasts the lesson. Present: four. Absent: two. One since the cold, one since the road closed. I am not removing them. A register with names struck out has decided something it has no authority to decide. If either of you hears this, the lesson is on the slate and I will read it again tomorrow at the same hour.

AUTOMATED EMERGENCY BEACON ARRAY. 142.85. TELETYPE FOLLOWS. [A synthesizer with no inflection, characters arriving at a fixed rate.] ASH FRONT BEARING TWO NINE ZERO. VELOCITY ELEVEN KILOMETRES PER HOUR. PARTICULATE LOAD RISING. VISIBILITY FORECAST BELOW ONE KILOMETRE AT SIX HOURS. SHELTER INTAKES. SECURE LOOSE MATERIAL. THIS MESSAGE REPEATS UNTIL SUPERSEDED. NO OPERATOR IS PRESENT. NO OPERATOR IS REQUIRED.

AUTOMATED EMERGENCY BEACON ARRAY. 142.85. STATUS. [Two pings, then teletype.] BANK STATE: TWENTY-TWO PERCENT. TRANSMIT POWER REDUCED TO HOLD SCHEDULE. PROJECTED SERVICE: ONE HUNDRED FORTY DAYS. THIS ARRAY WILL NOT ANNOUNCE ITS FINAL TRANSMISSION. THE FINAL TRANSMISSION WILL SIMPLY BE THE LAST ONE. SERVICE PARTY: NORTH MAST; HATCH TAKES A STANDARD KEY. THE ARRAY DOES NOT REQUEST SERVICE. THE ARRAY REPORTS.

CONTINUITY CHANNEL. AUTOMATED ARRAY 142.85. [Teletype.] STATION POLL. CIVIL DEFENSE: ABSENT. GARRISON TACTICAL: PRESENT, INTERMITTENT. OPEN AIRWAYS: PRESENT, HUMAN OPERATOR. CRATER RIM: PRESENT, UNREGISTERED FORMAT. NUMBERS ARRAY, SHORTWAVE: NOT POLLABLE FROM THIS BAND. [Four seconds.] FOUR OF SIX ANSWER. THE POLL REPEATS EVERY SIX HOURS. THE ARRAY HAS NO AUTHORITY TO CONCLUDE ANYTHING. THE ARRAY CONTINUES.

[A flat voice, no accent, no breath where breath should be. A music box plays three notes before the first group and three after the last.] SEVEN. TWO. NINE. FOUR. ONE. [Pause.] THREE. THREE. EIGHT. ZERO. SIX. [Pause.] SEVEN. TWO. NINE. FOUR. ONE. [The groups repeat for nine minutes without deviation. Then, once, breaking the pattern:] RAIL. CUT. [Two notes. Carrier drops.]

[The flat voice, shorter than the others; it contains no groups.] SCHEDULE NOTICE. THIS STATION TRANSMITS ON THE NINTH NIGHT. TEN MINUTES AFTER THE HOUR. THE SCHEDULE HAS BEEN KEPT FOR EIGHT HUNDRED SIX TRANSMISSIONS. THE SCHEDULE WILL BE KEPT. IF YOU HAVE ANSWERED THIS STATION, YOU HAVE CHANGED THE SCHEDULE, AND THE SCHEDULE HAS CHANGED FOR YOU. [Three notes. Carrier drops.]

[Music box, three notes. The voice reads at a pace meant for a hand writing it down.] FOUR ONE NINE. WATER, MUNICIPAL RESERVE, SEALED. [Pause.] TWO TWO SEVEN. WATER, MUNICIPAL RESERVE, SEALED. [Pause.] EIGHT ZERO THREE. DO NOT. [Three times, in the tone of the numbers, with no change of any kind.] EIGHT ZERO THREE. DO NOT. [Pause.] THREE ONE FIVE. CISTERNS, SIX ACCESS, FIVE SEALED, ONE MARKED. [Carrier drops.]
